newsitem.title: USA: Hunger will persist without focus on distribution.
newsitem.headline: Hunger will persist without focus on distribution.

text.p: Hundreds of millions of people will be malnourished for decades unless the world recognizes its obligations to the poor, former World Bank President Robert McNamara said on Tuesday.

"This issue of access to food is as important as the production of food and it receives very, very little attention," said McNamara, who called food access a "societal responsibility" that was ignored worldwide.

An estimated 750 million people are malnourished globally and the future "holds more of the same," he said, not because of lagging food output but because of a lack of interest in how it will be distributed.
"I'll guarantee you there will be massive hunger across the world in the year 2020 ..." McNamara said at a news conference to name the winners of the World Food Prize.

"If today the people in the richest country in the world (the United States) aren't sufficiently concerned about feeding the poor amongst them, why should we expect the people of India, the people of Pakistan, China, particularly sub-Saharan Africa, to be concerned about the hungry amongst them?"

Food access should be a key topic for discussion at next month's World Food Summit in Rome, he said. He said he hoped to discuss the matter this week with Jacques Diouf, head of the U.N. Food and Agriculture Organization. Both were to speak Saturday at a forum on food security in Des Moines, Iowa.

An FAO spokesman in Washington said food access would be on the agenda for the Rome meeting. "Access is clearly critical. There are many aspects to food security as well as production," the spokesman said.

Three recent U.S. steps have increased the likelihood of hunger domestically and worldwide, McNamara said. He cited the new welfare bill that reduced funding for social programs, cuts in support for agricultural research and "sharp cutbacks" in U.S. donations to international family planning programs.
